pack.title: Everyday Echoes
pack.description: Fresh connections hiding in familiar things.

categories.title: BREAKFAST BAKES
categories.triviaFact: A bagel is traditionally boiled before baking, which helps create its chewy crust.

categories.title: KITCHEN UTENSILS
categories.triviaFact: A ladle has a deep bowl designed for lifting and serving liquids such as soup.

categories.title: TENNIS TERMS
categories.triviaFact: In tennis scoring, love means zero and deuce is a tie at forty points each.

categories.title: PAIRS WITH JAM
categories.triviaFact: Logjam originated as a term for timber obstructing waterways before becoming a metaphor.

redHerrings.note: SERVE could describe offering breakfast, but LOVE, DEUCE and VOLLEY give it a precise tennis home.

categories.title: SEATS AROUND THE HOUSE
categories.triviaFact: A stool differs from a typical chair by having no backrest.

categories.title: IN A SEWING BASKET
categories.triviaFact: A thimble protects a fingertip while pushing a needle through fabric.

categories.title: PARTS OF A RIVER
categories.triviaFact: A river mouth is where the flowing water enters another body of water.

categories.title: BEFORE LIGHT
categories.triviaFact: The word spotlight expanded from stage lighting to mean public attention.

redHerrings.note: BED looks at home among household furniture, but the four actual seats leave it with the river terms.

categories.title: CITRUS FRUIT
categories.triviaFact: The colored outer layer of citrus peel contains aromatic oils used in zest.

categories.title: PARTS OF A PRINTED BOOK
categories.triviaFact: An index points readers to topics by page number rather than presenting the chapters in order.

categories.title: ISLAND COUNTRIES
categories.triviaFact: Japan is an archipelago, meaning a country spread across a group of islands.

categories.title: BEFORE CASE
categories.triviaFact: A staircase takes its name from the structure that encloses or supports its steps.

redHerrings.note: BOOK tempts you toward SPINE and COVER; it is the whole object, while its intended partners make words ending in CASE.

categories.title: TOOLS IN A WORKSHOP
categories.triviaFact: A wrench applies torque to turn fasteners such as nuts and bolts.

categories.title: SOUND LIKE LETTER NAMES
categories.triviaFact: Queue comes from a French word for a tail, a fitting image for a waiting line.

categories.title: CHESS PIECES
categories.triviaFact: A pawn that reaches the far end of the board can be promoted to another piece.

categories.title: BEFORE BOARD
categories.triviaFact: A dashboard originally shielded carriage passengers from mud kicked up by horses.

redHerrings.note: QUEEN and BEE suggest a hive, but there are no four bee-colony roles; the complete chess set resolves QUEEN.

categories.title: PASTA SHAPES
categories.triviaFact: Farfalle takes its Italian name from butterflies, reflected in its pinched shape.

categories.title: BANKING TRANSACTIONS
categories.triviaFact: A deposit adds funds to an account, while a withdrawal takes funds out.

categories.title: LAUNDRY ACTIONS
categories.triviaFact: A washing machine spins to expel water through holes in its drum.

categories.title: BEFORE NOTE
categories.triviaFact: A footnote lets a writer add detail without interrupting the main passage.

redHerrings.note: BANK suggests the financial actions, but is not itself a transaction; FOOT, END and KEY all take NOTE after them.

categories.title: PUBLIC TRANSPORT VEHICLES
categories.triviaFact: A ferry carries passengers or vehicles over a regular route across water.

categories.title: METRIC PREFIXES
categories.triviaFact: The prefix centi means one hundredth of the base unit.

categories.title: THINGS WITH TEETH
categories.triviaFact: Interlocking teeth allow gears to transfer rotation between shafts.

categories.title: BEFORE STOP
categories.triviaFact: A shortstop is a defensive position in baseball between second and third base.

redHerrings.note: BUS stop is a familiar phrase, but BUS has three exact transport partners; the STOP group includes NON, as in nonstop.

categories.title: BAKING MEASURES
categories.triviaFact: An ounce can measure mass, while a fluid ounce measures volume.

categories.title: PARTS OF A SHOE
categories.triviaFact: The tongue of a laced shoe cushions the top of the foot beneath the laces.

categories.title: SEEN ON A MAP
categories.triviaFact: Contour lines connect points of equal elevation on a map.

categories.title: COOKING WORDS THAT ARE ALSO PEOPLE
categories.triviaFact: Julienne names both a French given name and a cut that makes thin strips.

redHerrings.note: SCALE could sit among kitchen measuring equipment, but the baking group contains units, leaving SCALE with map features.

categories.title: TYPES OF KNOT
categories.triviaFact: A bowline makes a fixed loop that does not tighten like a slip knot.

categories.title: WORDS FOR A SMALL AMOUNT
categories.triviaFact: A pinch is an informal amount that can be held between finger and thumb.

categories.title: DOUBLE AS VERBS FOR MOVING QUICKLY
categories.triviaFact: Bolt can mean both a metal fastener and a sudden rapid movement.

categories.title: FOLLOW BLACK
categories.triviaFact: A blacksmith traditionally works iron, which forms a dark oxide coating when heated.

redHerrings.note: BOLT can be a quantity of cloth, tempting a measures connection, but DASH, PINCH, DROP and TRACE all mean a small amount.
